To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a mutant yeast cell arrested at meiosis I has synapsed homologous chromosomes, but lacks the central element of the synaptonemal complex.
a mutant of the cdc5 gene, when grown at the nonpermissive (34°C) temperature, arrests meiosis after premeiotic replication and before haploidisation.

the CDC5 gene product is required for meiosis I and II in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and that the arrest of meiosis in the cdc5- 1 mutant at the first division results in elevated recombination and unusual synaptonemal complex-like structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the genetic control of meiotic recombination and chromosome pairing in yeast, and the relationship between these events and the cell cycle.
the role of the CDC5 function in meiosis and with the nature of the meiotic arrest.
the molecular basis of the meiosis-specific function of the CDC5 gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cdc5- 1 is required for the normal completion of both meiotic divisions.
the CDC5 gene product is required for the completion of meiosis in yeast.
the CDC5 gene product is required for the completion of meiotic chromosome pairing and recombination and that its function is not required for the initiation of these processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CDC5 is required for the completion of meiosis, and is not required for recombination commitment.
CDC5 is required for the completion of both meiotic divisions.
the CDC5 gene product is required for both meiotic divisions, but not for recombination commitment, and that the arrest of meiosis at 34°C is not due to a failure of recombination commitment.

the CDC5 gene product is involved in the regulation of meiosis in yeast.
